title: memory/incidents/<id>.json - one authored incident claim (G17, decision 50)
description: ⛔ THE INCIDENT LIBRARY OWNS A SIGNATURE, ITS CAUSE AND ITS FIX, ONCE (the memo's single-sourcing rule). A lesson promoted from this incident's candidate cites the incident id as provenance and NEVER copies the fix body; a log row that triggered it points at the id; nobody restates signature/cause/fix. TRACKED (committed, survives a clone) unlike the machine-local ops log: an incident is project knowledge, written through core/_io.js writeAtomicJSON by the `incident` verb and read back through readJSONClassified. The three texts and the author are required and non-empty - a blank one is refused before the record is written. `incident --new` mints one root-cause-fix candidate in the same call whose claim names the incident by id (never the fix), recorded here as `candidateId`; a verb only ever edits an existing record to close it (`status`, `closedAt`, `closedBy`), never to rewrite the signature, cause or fix.

signature.description: How the incident is recognised next time - one authored claim.

cause.description: What caused it - one authored claim.

fix.description: What fixed it - one authored claim. Lives here ONCE; a promoted lesson cites the id, never this body.

cycleId.description: The source revision the incident was authored at, resolved the way the savepoint resolves it.

logRefs.description: Digests of the ops-log rows that triggered this incident - pointers only.

candidateId.description: The root-cause-fix candidate minted for this incident (cm_...), or null if the mint could not land.

closedAt.description: When the incident was closed (status fixed) - the one edit a verb makes.
